title: Death in Custody Reporting Act of 2013
official_summary:
(This measure has not been amended since it was introduced. The expanded summary of the House reported version is repeated here.)

Death in Custody Reporting Act of 2013 - Requires states that receive allocations under specified provisions of the Omnibus Crime Control and Safe Streets Act of 1968, whether characterized as the Edward Byrne Memorial State and Local Law Enforcement Assistance Programs, the Local Government Law Enforcement Block Grants Program, the Edward Byrne Memorial Justice Assistance Grant Program, or otherwise, to report to the Attorney General on a quarterly basis certain information regarding the death of any person who is detained, arrested, en route to incarceration, or incarcerated in state or local facilities or a boot camp prison. Imposes penalties on states that fail to comply with such reporting requirements..

Requires the head of each federal law enforcement agency to report to the Attorney General annually certain information regarding the death of any person who: (1) is detained or arrested by any officer of such agency (or by any state or local law enforcement officer for purposes of a federal law enforcement operation); or (2) is en route to be incarcerated or detained, or is incarcerated or detained, at any federal correctional facility or federal pretrial detention facility located within the United States or any other facility pursuant to a contract with or used by such agency.

Requires the Attorney General to study such information and report on means by which it can be used to reduce the number of such deaths.

summary.headline: This 2014 law requires states and federal agencies to report deaths of people held in custody to the Attorney General, who must study the reports.
summary.what_it_does: States that receive certain federal crime-control grants must report to the Attorney General each quarter about deaths of people who are detained, arrested, being taken to prison, or incarcerated in state or local facilities. Each federal law enforcement agency must report similar deaths to the Attorney General once a year, including deaths in federal prisons and detention centers. The Attorney General must study the reports and recommend ways to reduce these deaths. States that do not comply can face penalties.

who_it_affects.group: States that receive certain federal Byrne or Justice Assistance grants
who_it_affects.how: They must send the Attorney General quarterly reports on deaths in their custody or face penalties for not complying.

who_it_affects.group: State and local jails, prisons, and law enforcement agencies
who_it_affects.how: Their deaths of detained or incarcerated people are included in the required state reporting to the federal government.

who_it_affects.group: Heads of federal law enforcement agencies
who_it_affects.how: Each must report deaths of people detained or arrested by their officers to the Attorney General once a year.

who_it_affects.group: People held in federal correctional or pretrial detention facilities
who_it_affects.how: Deaths of people in these facilities, or in contracted facilities, are covered by the federal annual reporting requirement.
The office must collect these reports, study them, and report on ways to use the data to reduce custody deaths.

summary.when_it_takes_effect: Enacted December 18, 2014; the summary does not list separate effective dates for the reporting requirements.
